what: Text around the cursor looks like it’s seen through a glass lens — only while the cursor moves or presses, lens (diameter = screen height 26% × 2, radius 120~300px) up to four texts within it get an SVG refraction filter. The lens center pushes letters outward (strength = radius × .16 × response) with a soft ripple (.014) mixed in around it. Response is cursor speed × .9 (follows at 12 per second when rising and 2.4 when settling), .5 while pressed, and 1.3 at the moment of the press, decaying at 1.8 per second, and at that moment the lens swells to double size and returns. When the cursor stops, the filter is removed so the text becomes sharp.

options.size: Lens radius (share of screen height, clamped to 120–300px), default .26

from.where: index.html .rw-rail__ink·.rw-epi__block p (first section’s large title lines and closing text lines — original [data-glass] with glass-type-0~3 filters: feImage lens map 128px, feTurbulence .014×2, k3 .25+.55·kick+.2·move, scale .16·r·amt)

note: There are four filter cells, so at most four shimmer at once (in document order, not by proximity). Not applied on devices without a pointer or with reduced motion
